headline: Revenue grows on fleet expansion but profit slips
summary_short: Revenue rose 9.2% y/y to $2,184.2M, but operating income fell 5.8% to $569.9M as cruise operating expenses grew 18.8%. Diluted EPS was $1.11 versus $1.15 a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue grew on added fleet capacity and higher revenue per passenger cruise day, partly offset by lower occupancy after guest cancellations tied to low water on some European rivers. Operating margin was 26.1% against 30.2%. Nine-month operating cash flow was $1,724.6M, investment in vessels and intangibles was $1,323.6M, and $350.0M of shares were repurchased. Cash ended at $4,052.3M. This filing is interim financials only; no guidance is given.
confidence_notes: IFRS interim condensed financial statements (6-K); the separate MD&A exhibit was not reached, so Adjusted EBITDA, net yield and occupancy are not captured. Shard EPS $1.11 matches reported diluted EPS; the shard y/y prior ($0.99) does not match the reported $1.15, so the reported figure is used. Q3 is a seasonal peak, so the q/q EPS drop from $1.32 is not read as a trend.

drivers.explanation: Growth came from added capacity from the fleet and higher revenue per passenger cruise day, partly offset by lower Q3 occupancy from cancellations linked to low water levels on some European rivers.
Cruise operating expenses grew 18.8% against revenue growth of 9.2%, compressing operating margin to 26.1% from 30.2%.
